variants.headline: Builder signs for a new project
variants.sub: A construction contract for {project} has been awarded to {builder}.
variants.body:
The builder {builder} has signed a contract for {project} at an agreed price of {price}. The signature establishes an undertaking to build, not a completed building. Readers assessing {target} should distinguish the award from delivery, while taking seriously the obligations the agreement is meant to create.

Construction is work, not simply a promise taking shape on paper. Labour should keep the people doing that work in view when a contract is celebrated. An agreed price gives the undertaking terms; it should not become an excuse to treat decent conditions or practical responsibility as somebody else's concern.

The handling of {target} should be assessed against the signed undertaking. This paper records the award and agreed price without announcing a construction result that the contract itself has not yet delivered. Ordinary lives should be the measure, not a convenient afterthought.
